title: The crucial role of ecohydraulic factors in triggering sturgeon reproduction: Implications for active habitat restoration strategies in the Yangtze River
content:
Our study underscores the importance of ecohydraulic conditions in triggering spawning activities of sturgeon and provides a theoretical foundation for restoration actions to revive Yangtze sturgeon populations. We highlight the need for adjusting the current conservation policy in the Yangtze Basin by allowing active habitat restoration in nature reserves and optimizing hydropower operations to revive sturgeon populations. Evidence provided by our study offers a replicable model for the conservation of migratory fish, emphasizing the potential of active habitat restoration strategies to revive populations of endangered fish species in the Yangtze Basin.


Abstract

Sturgeons and paddlefishes (Acipenseriformes) are among the most threatened species worldwide. In the Yangtze River, all three Acipenseriformes species are either extinct or have failed natural reproduction and recruitment due to overfishing and habitat destruction. Although many conservation measures have been implemented, no natural reproduction of the Yangtze sturgeon (Acipenser dabryanus) has been observed in the wild since 2000. New conservation and restoration actions are urgently needed to save sturgeons from extinction in the Yangtze River. We established large-scale ecohydraulic modelling over 600 km of the upper Yangtze River to identify the critical conditions that support sturgeon reproduction. Based on the theoretical modelling results, we conducted indoor experiments to optimize the combinations of identified key ecohydraulic parameters. Furthermore, we tested the efficacy of these optimized conditions for triggering sturgeon spawning with reconstructed habitat in the Yangtze River. Ecohydraulic conditions triggering sturgeon reproduction were jointly influenced by water velocity and riverbed morphology, including substrate grain size and riverbed slope. Theoretical modelling of historical conditions and indoor experiments revealed that suitable spawning grounds of the Yangtze sturgeon were characterized by pool–riffle sequences with fast flow and coarse substrates. Our reconstructed habitats in the Yangtze River successfully triggered spawning activities of the Yangtze sturgeon, resulting in fertilized eggs and hatched fry. In addition, we demonstrated that hydropower plants altered the ecohydrological conditions of historical spawning grounds of sturgeons in the Yangtze River, adversely affecting their reproduction and recruitment. Synthesis and applications. Our study underscores the importance of ecohydraulic conditions in triggering spawning activities of sturgeon and provides a theoretical foundation for restoration actions to revive Yangtze sturgeon populations. We highlight the need for adjusting the current conservation policy in the Yangtze Basin by allowing active habitat restoration in nature reserves and optimizing hydropower operations to revive sturgeon populations. Evidence provided by our study offers a replicable model for the conservation of migratory fish, emphasizing the potential of active habitat restoration strategies to revive populations of endangered fish species in the Yangtze Basin.

摘要

鲟形目鱼类(鲟科和白鲟科)是全球受威胁最严重的物种之一。长江中的三种鲟鱼或因过度捕捞和栖息地破坏而灭绝，或已无法进行自然繁殖和种群补充。尽管已经实施了许多保护措施，但自2000年以来，人们在野外再未观察到长江鲟的自然繁殖。迫切需要采取新的保护和恢复行动，以拯救长江中的鲟鱼免遭灭绝。 我们构建了覆盖长江上游600多公里历史产卵场范围内的大规模生态水力学模型，以确定诱发鲟鱼自然繁殖的关键生态水力学条件。基于理论建模结果，我们不仅通过室内实验获取了诱导长江鲟繁殖的最佳生态水力学参数，还在长江天然水域重建的产卵栖息地中测试了这些条件触发鲟鱼产卵的有效性。 触发鲟鱼繁殖的生态水力学条件受水流速度和河床形态(包括底质粒径和河床坡度)的共同影响。对历史产卵场环境条件的理论建模和室内实验表明，长江鲟适宜的产卵场均具有深潭-浅滩序列、水流速度快和底质粗糙的特点。 通过在长江天然水中实施了产卵生境营造成功触发了长江鲟的自然繁殖行为，使其产下受精卵并孵化出鱼苗。同时，研究证明水电站修建改变了长江鲟历史产卵场的生态水力条件，对其繁殖产生不利影响。 综合与应用:本研究强调了生态水力学条件在触发鲟鱼产卵活动中的重要性，为长江鲟种群恢复重建提供了理论基础。我们强调了调整长江流域当前保护政策的必要性，允许在自然保护区内进行积极的栖息地修复行动，包括优化水电运行以提供适宜生态流量条件，助力长江鲟种群恢复。本研究强调积极栖息地恢复策略在恢复长江流域濒危鱼类种群方面的巨大潜力，可为其它濒危鱼类保护提供参考。
